single_43937_20260731_173214.question_text: Will the US and India finalise a new bilateral trade agreement before August 2026?
single_43937_20260731_173214.refresh_reason: manual single refresh (community prediction shift alert)
single_43937_20260731_173214.reasoning:
(a) Time left until resolution: Today is July 31, 2026, and the resolution deadline is August 1, 2026. There is approximately 1 day left.

(b) Status quo outcome if nothing changes: No deal has been finalized/signed as of July 31, 2026. The status quo is NO resolution.

(c) Scenario for NO outcome: The most likely scenario — the deal has not been signed before August 1, 2026. The research indicates a US official said the deal could be signed in "3-4 months" (from roughly mid-June, placing it in September-October 2026). The Section 301 investigations are still pending, India's Commerce Minister said it will only operate when India gains comparative advantage. No announcement of signing has occurred.

(d) Scenario for YES outcome: India's trade minister Piyush Goyal said in early June that a first tranche could be concluded by mid-July. If this happened and I'm simply missing the announcement, it would resolve YES. However, the current research (which appears current as of late July) still describes the deal as pending and future-oriented ("will be signed at the right time," "3-4 months").

(e) Base rate: No reliable base rate available — proceeding on priors. Trade deals between major economies typically take years to finalize; interim/tranche deals can move faster, but even preliminary deals often slip past initial deadlines.

(f) How the live data moves me: The research is quite clear: as of the most recent available information, the deal has NOT been signed. Key signals:
- "Framework deal is ready to be inked at the right time" — not yet signed
- "Deal could be signed in 3-4 months" from a US official — pushing timeline to September-October 2026
- Section 301 investigations still pending as a blocking factor
- India's minister saying it will operate "once India gets comparative advantage" — suggesting no imminent signing
- The July 24 tariff deadline has passed with new Section 301 tariffs being introduced, not a trade deal
- No announcement of a signed deal appears anywhere in the research

(g) How my view has changed: The original 68% forecast was presumably made when talks were accelerating and mid-July was the stated target. Now, with July 31 being the final day before resolution and no deal signed (the research consistently describes it as future-oriented), the probability has collapsed dramatically. The community has moved from ~68% to 2%, reflecting that the mid-July target was missed and the deal is now pushed to 3-4 months out.

(h) Community prediction divergence: The community is at 2%. I fully agree with this assessment. With less than 24 hours until resolution and no evidence of a signed deal (in fact, strong evidence pointing to a September-October timeline), the probability of resolution YES is extremely low. A last-minute surprise announcement on July 31 cannot be ruled out entirely (hence not 0%), but it would be extraordinary given all signals point to the deal being weeks to months away. The community's 2% appropriately captures this tiny residual probability.

Probability: 2%
single_43937_20260731_173214.research_text:
A bilateral trade agreement (BTA) between the US and India is nearing completion, with officials from both countries indicating that the "framework deal is ready" and will be signed at the "right time" [economictimes.indiatimes.com](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/foreign-trade/us-framework-trade-deal-ready-to-be-inked-at-the-right-time-commerce-secretary-rajesh-agrawal/articleshow/132375864.cms). A senior US official stated on Wednesday that a deal could be signed within three to four months, suggesting virtual completion of negotiations [economictimes.indiatimes.com](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/foreign-trade/us-india-trade-deal-could-be-signed-in-3-4-months-us-official-says/articleshow/132556710.cms).

However, the finalization is pending the conclusion of US Section 301 trade investigations, particularly regarding allegations of forced labor and excess industrial capacity involving 60 economies, including India [economictimes.indiatimes.com](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/foreign-trade/us-india-trade-deal-could-be-signed-in-3-4-months-us-official-says/articleshow/132556710.cms), [timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/to-be-signed-at-right-time-india-us-trade-deal-framework-ready-says-official/articleshow/132368260.cms). While a previous 10% global tariff expired on July 24, Washington introduced new tariffs under Section 301, proposing up to 12.5% on dozens of nations, including India, which will face a new 10% duty [financialexpress.com](https://www.financialexpress.com/india-news/india-us-trade-deal-as-july-24-tariff-deadline-nears-expert-says-trump-lost-the-bargaining-chip/4301243/). India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has emphasized that the deal will only operate once India gains a comparative advantage over competitors [economictimes.indiatimes.com](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/foreign-trade/india-us-trade-pact-to-come-into-operation-once-india-gets-comparative-advantage-piyush-goyal/articleshow/132716938.cms).
